chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever is unable to connect with us, let him connect with the poor of our Shias; and whoever is unable to visit our graves, let him visit the pious among our brothers."

key_terms.فُقَرَاءَ شِيعَتِنَا: the poor of our Shia community

ai.seo_question: How can one connect with the Imams if they cannot visit them personally?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor and Major Ghaibah, this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes a mechanism for maintaining spiritual connectivity (wasilah) when direct access to the Imam is obstructed. It elevates the status of the pious community (al-salihin) as living extensions of the Imams, thereby transforming social support and communal visitation into acts of devotion equivalent to visiting the Imams themselves.
